metadata.title: Claude, Matter Close.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: does closing a matter delete it? Take the skill apart, explain how it archives the record out of the active portfolio without deleting it — capturing only what the file tells it to — and judge the design choice (reversibility over cleanliness).

beats.narration_text: Liam here, in for Bear. Someone asked: can Claude delete a closed matter? No — the skill archives it. It pulls the record out of your active list and keeps it. Here is what actually runs.

beats.narration_text: Here is what a skill actually is: a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is matter-close. The whole instruction set sits in one file — SKILL.md, plain language, no hidden logic, no code path you cannot inspect. They optimized for legibility over cleverness. The file is the program.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in the Steps section. Claude reads each step in order, then runs it. Linear — no branching unless a step says so. What that buys you is predictability; what it costs is cleverness. Same request in, same trace out.

Here is the interesting constraint. Capture three things — outcome, final exposure, lessons. Archive the record out of your active portfolio. Never delete it. They chose reversibility over cleanliness: the archive stays lightly cluttered, but nothing you might need later is gone. Same scope in, same shape out, every time.

props.sparkLine: Same scope, same result, every time.

beats.narration_text: The carry-out. Closing a matter archives it out of the active list, every time — the record survives. What lands in the archive is only what the file says to capture. The file is the boundary; the file is the promise.

props.quote: Closing a matter archives it out of the active list, every time — it never deletes the record. What gets captured is only what the file tells it to.
props.sparkLine: Archived, not deleted — scoped to the file.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. I want to close a completed legal matter. Here's the matter — paste your summary in. Walk me through it step by step: one, the outcome — how did it resolve, in one sentence? Two, the final exposure — money paid, money at risk, obligations that outlive closure? Three, three lessons a future matter like this one should carry forward. Then draft the archive record as a short markdown file — outcome, exposure, lessons, plus the smallest set of pointers I would need to reopen it. Do not delete anything; do not summarize away detail I might need. Go deeper: ask the same model what changes if this matter is subject to a seven-year privilege-log retention rule — what does the archive record need to include that it would not otherwise?
